target_claim: The reduction maps yes-instances of 3-Partition to yes-instances of 12Partition; in particular the constructed subsets A_j (all four copies of the three elements of T_j) all have the same sum.
source_quote: where Cj depends only on the indices. Since each index appears in exactly one partition set, all Aj have the same sum.
test_sketch: Implement construction (1): for each t_i build s^(j)_i = t_i + j*K*4^(3m+1-i), j=1..4, K=1+mB. Take a yes-instance of 3-Partition with m=2, e.g. T=(5,5,6,5,5,6), B=16 (valid 3-partition {t1,t2,t3},{t4,t5,t6}, each summing to 16). Compute sum(A1)=4*16+10K*(4^6+4^5+4^4) and sum(A2)=4*16+10K*(4^3+4^2+4^1); they differ, directly refuting the quoted equal-sum claim. Additionally, a brute-force oracle enumerating all C(24,12)/2 partitions of S into two 12-element subsets finds no equal-sum partition, showing the reduction maps a yes-instance to a no-instance, so the reduction (and hence the claimed iff) is wrong.
